candidates.phrase: the Father is the Source of all that exists
candidates.rationale: Calls the Father 'the Source of all that exists,' asserting ultimate origin-status not derived from another, a source-status proposition within the floor though short of an explicit denial of generation.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe the Father is the Source of all that exists, whether of matter or spirit. With the Son and the Holy Spirit, He made man, male and female, in His image. By intention He relates to people as Father, thereby forever declaring His goodwill toward them. In love, He both seeks and receives penitent sinners.

candidates.locator: Article I — Of Faith in the Holy Trinity
candidates.phrase: the maker and preserver of all things, both visible and invisible
candidates.rationale: Names the one true God as maker and preserver of all things, implying underived source-status consistent with the floor, but does not explicitly deny generation from another.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one living and true God, everlasting, without body or parts, of infinite power, wisdom, and goodness; the maker and preserver of all things, both visible and invisible. And in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

candidates.phrase: Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible
candidates.rationale: Describes the one true God as Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things, implying He is the uncaused source of all, a partial overlap with the Unbegotten floor.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one true, holy and living God, Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible. He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love, and rules with gracious regard for the well-being and salvation of men, to the glory of his name. We believe the one God reveals himself as the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power.

sonnet.floor_reason: The passage asserts the Father as Source of all that exists in the context of creation (with the Son and Holy Spirit making man), which touches source-status but does not explicitly deny the Father's generation from another within the Godhead.
sonnet.reason: Verbatim and correctly subjected assertion naming the Father specifically, but the surrounding context frames 'Source' relationally toward creation rather than metaphysically as denial of generation from another divine person.
